answer: Sybil resistance here relies on quadratic stake: an agent locks capital to earn voting weight, but that weight is the square root of its bond, not the bond itself. Splitting one hoard into k identities gives k times sqrt of S/k, or sqrt of kS, votes while costing k times S, so influence grows only as the square root of expense. A raider chasing tenfold sway must lock a hundredfold, and clones caught coordinating forfeit the entire bond. Whether it calls itself marble, meadow or yarrow, each persona needs its own funded stake, so one wealthy operator cannot pass as a crowd.
